title: introduce-invocation-context-fingerprinter-and-alert-squelch-fabric
text:
introduce-invocation-context-fingerprinter-and-alert-squelch-fabric

description:
Motivation: noisy per-tenant SLO alerts and expensive wide-context joins were making incident triage slow for teams that operate multi-tenant workloads. This PR introduces an Invocation Context Fingerprinter (ICF) and a lightweight Alert Squelch Fabric (ASF) to reduce alert churn and enable low-latency correlation of token-cost/latency signals across anonymized tenants. Design summary: the ICF computes a stable, privacy-preserving 128-bit fingerprint for each invocation by hashing a compact context vector (route id, prompt-shape hash, first-2-token-signature, kernel-path-id) and a locality-sensitive sketch of the first N token embeddings to capture structural similarity without retaining raw PII. Fingerprints are stored as 64-bit hex in ClickHouse column invocation_fingerprint with a TTL and approximate cardinality rollup. The ASF consults a cohort registry that groups fingerprints by entropy and recent error-rate similarity, and applies time-decayed suppression rules to transient alert spikes for cohorts that have high within-group homogeneity. Implementation highlights: - New package telemetry/icf implementing LSH + XXHash-based stable folding, with deterministic tests. - ClickHouse migration: add invocation_fingerprint, cohort_id, and a per-invocation token_cost_histogram (compact 8-bucket time-decayed histogram) for fast per-route rollups. - Observability API: new endpoint GET /v1/observability/fingerprints/{route} to retrieve recent cohort summaries and representative fingerprints. - Console: Dashboard panels added to Observability Console: Invocation Fingerprint Matrix, Cohort Token-Cost Heatmap, and Alert Squelch Monitor. - CLI: redwoodctl observability enable-fingerprinter --route <route> and redwoodctl observability cohort-dump. - Runtime integration: the runtime attaches the fingerprint to existing traces as trace tag fingerprint.hex and to spans as marginal tag icf.bucket. - Backwards compatibility: feature gated via env REDWOOD_ICF_ENABLED and per-tenant opt-in toggle; if disabled, nothing is written to ClickHouse and traces include a placeholder tag. Testing: unit tests cover LSH stability across seeds and simulated embedding noise, ClickHouse migration tested in staging with a compact dataset, e2e smoke validates that enabling ICF does not materially change per-request latency (median overhead measured at +0.6ms on p3.2xlarge). Load test: cohort rollups were exercised with a 10k rps synthetic workload in perf-lab and show 0.4% increase in storage read traffic thanks to compact histograms. Observability: added prometheus metrics telemetry_icf_processed_total, telemetry_icf_sketch_entropy, and asf_suppressed_alerts_total with labels (route, cohort). Alert tuning: new alert policy ASF-FLAP-01 suppresses repeated high-latency alerts for cohorts that meet suppression criteria (min_invocations=50 in window, entropy<0.25, no error-rate increase). Rollout plan: gate on REDWOOD_ICF_ENABLED, enable for internal tenants for 48h, monitor telemetry_icf_sketch_entropy and asf_suppressed_alerts_total, then progressive enable for external beta tenants.

Review conversation:
Miguel Torres: Nice design, the LSH sketch looks compact. Question: how deterministic is the fingerprint across different embedding implementations?
Aisha Khan: We use an L2-normalized float16 sketch with deterministic seed folding; tests include fuzzed embedding variants to validate stability within acceptable epsilon.
Samir Patel: Concern: adding columns to ClickHouse could increase query complexity for high-cardinality tenants. Suggest adding a TTL and sampled materialized view for costly joins.
Aisha Khan: Added TTL (30d) and a sampled materialized view in migration; updated the console panels to query the MV for heatmap generation.
Claire Zhang: Please add an opt-out at tenant-level and ensure KMS keys are not used to derive fingerprints (do not store raw user identifiers).
Aisha Khan: Confirmed tenant opt-out flag implemented and fingerprint is one-way hashed from non-PII features only.
Miguel Torres: CI failure on first run (go vet + staticcheck) — some unused imports in sketch_test.go
Aisha Khan: Fixed unused imports and rebased; CI passed on rerun.
Samir Patel: Approved pending small docs tweak to explain suppression hysteresis
Claire Zhang: Approved — merging when green.

Release notes:
Adds Invocation Context Fingerprinter (ICF) and Alert Squelch Fabric (ASF). ICF provides a compact, privacy-preserving fingerprint for invocations enabling cohort-level rollups and faster cross-invocation correlation. ASF reduces noisy alert churn by suppressing transient spikes for homogenous cohorts. New dashboards, CLI commands, and metrics included. Feature is opt-in and disabled by default.

Additional notes:
migration includes a light-weight materialized view to avoid scanning raw events and a staged backfill strategy that writes fingerprints for a 7d sliding window initially. Operational playbook added to docs/observability/fingerprinter_playbook.md with runbook steps for unmuting suppressed cohorts and diagnosing false suppression.
